newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: RESEARCH ALERT - Kim Eng sees good buys in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Kim Eng sees good buys in Malaysia.

text.p: Recent panic selling caused by Malaysia's credit restrictions on share and property lending has opened a window of opportunity for selective stock purchases, Kim Eng Securities said in a strategy report.
The brokerage said in a note received by Reuters on Thursday that the correction has brought equity valuations to more reasonable levels.

Concerns over Malaysia's potentially destablising asset price inflation as reflected in rising property prices and banks' exposure to share financing led the Bank Negara to tighten lending to the two sectors on March 28.
The curbs require banks and finance companies to trim their exposure to the property sector to 20 percent of the total outstanding loans from nearly 30 percent.

The uncertainties over the new lending rules, coupled with major corrections on Wall Street, sent the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange into a tailspin. Its key composite index plummeted over 10 percent to hit a low of 1,086.67 on April 15.
"The focus is on oversold stocks which have good operating cash flow and balance sheet, supported by sound management," the Kim Eng report said.
"We remain underweight on commercial property segment and cautious on residential properties," it said.
Its caution over residential properties was based on sentiment that the sector would take time to adjust to the latest lending measures.
Its recommendations included Affin Holdings Bhd, which is unaffected by the restrictions, IJM Corporation Bhd, Road Builder (M) Holdings Bhd and Sungei Way Holdings Bhd.
It also recommended established contractors with a good order book and Malakoff Bhd, one of the cheapest exposure to the power sector.

Other recommendations were Tanjong Plc, Sime UEP Properties Bhd, Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd, PNE PCB Bhd and Telekom Malaysia Bhd based on their valuation relative to their growth potentials and the peers.
Kim Eng said it doubted the effectiveness of Malaysia's latest credit controls and believed domestic liquidity would remain flushed unless more aggressive measures were taken.
It added that the second board and second line stocks on the main board were likely beneficiaries of the domestic liquidity. -- Singapore newsroom (65 8703080)
